references.text: Moses commands the judges to kill those who had joined Baal-Peor, a similar situation where Israel's leaders had to execute judgment on idolaters.

The blessing of the tribe of Levi mentions that they showed no partiality toward their relatives, a reference to the incident with the golden calf where the Levites killed their own brothers and neighbors.
The law to kill idolaters, even if it is one's brother, son, daughter, wife, or friend, reflects the principle in Exodus 32:27.
Phinehas' zeal in killing an Israelite man and a Midianite woman demonstrates the same principle of executing judgment without regard for kinship.
Ezekiel's vision of men going through Jerusalem and striking down those who lack the mark resembles the Levites' mission to go from gate to gate and kill.
Jesus' words that whoever loves father or mother more than him is not worthy of him reflect the principle of putting God ahead of family loyalty.
Jesus' teaching to hate one's father, mother, wife, children, and siblings in order to be his disciple shows the same radical loyalty to God over family.
Exodus illustrates the concrete consequence of refusing the call to repentance described in 2 Kings.
